intro_en:
The Israel National Trail continues along the edge of the Naftali Hills with views over the Hula Valley. We climb to Keren Naftali and bid farewell to the valley scenery with a fine lookout from the summit.
From Keren Naftali the trail continues south through the Yahmur Valley and passes through farmland. We make our way to the descent into the Nahal Dishon streambed, where the trail climbs alongside the stream channel until it meets Road 886.
character_en: The trail follows hiking paths and vehicle tracks. Most of it is gentle, with a short climb and descent at Keren Naftali. The trail descends steeply to Nahal Dishon. The route is partly shaded.
parking_en: Convenient at the start and end of the segment
transport_en: Yesha Junction. There is no public transport to the end point
pois_en: Metzudat Koach (Koach Fortress), Nebi Yusha, Keren Naftali, Nahal Dishon
description_en:
From the parking area at the entrance to Metzudat Koach (Koach Fortress), we descend to Road 899. We cross the road carefully, and after a short walk we reach a domed building known as the tomb of Nebi Yusha. It is a remnant of a Shiite village that stood here until 1948.
The trail continues on a gentle course between planted forest trees and natural woodland. From time to time the view of the Hula Valley opens up to the east, and to the west the houses of Moshav Ramot Naftali. During the War of Independence the moshav held out against several attacks by local Arab forces.
After about an hour's walk we reach a vehicle track. We follow the track for a short stretch until we reach the foot of Keren Naftali, a hill whose dome-shaped summit is covered with pine trees. The climb to the summit is short. At the top, the trail passes through an archaeological site, an ancient military outpost next to an antenna compound. From here begins the descent from the 'Keren' (the Horn).
Before descending, it is worth heading to the eastern side of the summit, to a lookout with a beautiful view over the Hula Valley.
At the end of the descent we pass through a farming area: pastures, vineyards, poultry farms and orchards. Along the agricultural area the trail is gentle. A pedestrian gate through a cattle fence and a green nature reserve entrance sign mark the start of the descent into the Nahal Dishon streambed and the transition to natural scenery. The descent is short but a little steep.
Up the stream we walk along a comfortable jeep track. Beautiful natural woodland shades the trail all the way to the Road 886 bridge.
nearby_en: The Circassian Museum in Rihaniya, by prior arrangement only.
Alma Cave, 2.5 km each way along a jeep track; a challenging passage with flashlights inside the cave. Note: the cave is closed during the bats' hibernation, from 1 November to 15 June.
author_en: Itzik Ben Dov, Trail Marking Coordinator, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
